answer: Sybil farms fail when earning rights are tied to a unique berth that cannot be cloned. A name must post seasoned timber as collateral and keep a scheduled slot on a public harbor ledger for two settlements. Arrival proofs are checked only at one numbered jetty, in a window too short for two names to present the same hull, clock, or funding trail. If two arrivals share a wallet cluster or the same delayed-reveal cargo hash, both berths are slashed. One honest operator holds one slot at modest cost; extra names each need their own collateral and unshareable arrival window.
